title: Existence of a single perfect generator
statement: For every quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme X [def-pc-scheme], there exists a perfect complex M in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex] that is a generator in the sense of [def-pc-generators], and such that the smallest localizing, retract-closed full subcategory containing M is all of D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X).

source.place: Tag 09IS (perfect-remark-perfect-generator), existence of a single perfect generator

proof.text: Apply the supported perfect generator theorem with T = X. The empty complement is compact; all support conditions are vacuous. This gives a perfect object P of D_QCoh(X), the shifted-Hom detection equivalence, and the required triangulated structure.

The same P is compact. Apply the supported tower construction core with V empty, E = P and arbitrary target Y. Its support hypotheses are vacuous and its triangulated-closure hypothesis comes from the supported generator theorem. It supplies a tower starting at zero, transition triangles with coproducts of shifts of P as the third objects, and an ambient telescope triangle ending in Y. All indexing sets are in Type u, regardless of the derived morphism universe.

Let Q be any ambient triangulated, retract-closed property closed under Type u coproducts and containing P. Shift closure puts every P[m] in Q and coproduct closure puts each attaching sum in Q. The initial zero object lies in Q. Induction on the transition triangles, using triangulated closure of their middle object, puts every stage in Q. Reindex the countable coproduct by ULift ℕ in Type u and apply coproduct closure. Closure of the third object in the telescope triangle puts Y in Q. Retract closure is not needed. These are the defining closure properties and the coproduct index equivalence.
